active_learning.evidence: Session is mostly student attempts at MCQs (turns 71, 75, 79, 81, 83) with brief tutor scaffolding; minimal lecturing.

direct_instruction_active_practice.evidence: Each tutor instruction is followed by a student MCQ attempt (e.g., turn 78 explanation → turn 79 attempt), though some tutor turns mix two instructions before asking.

deliberate_practice.evidence: On the 190° error (turn 76), tutor gave corrective feedback, but then repeated essentially the same subtraction problem multiple times (turns 78, 80, 82) without varying the skill.

mastery_learning.evidence: After repeated arithmetic failures (turns 79, 81, 83), tutor announces 'You've got the method down' (turn 84) and moves on despite student never producing 170 themselves.

cognitive_load.evidence: Tutor broke subtraction into smaller steps in turn 82 ('360 - 100 = 260. Now, what is 260 - 90?'), reducing load.

layering.evidence: Turn 74 explicitly links the new problem to the just-mastered fact: 'angles around a point always sum to a full turn. Let's apply that rule.'

non_interference.evidence: Only one topic (angles around a point) covered; no confusable concepts introduced.

interleaving.evidence: All practice items are the same problem type (angles-at-a-point subtraction); no variation in problem structure.

testing_effect.evidence: Tutor asks student to attempt before revealing (e.g., turn 76 'Show me how you set up your calculation'); retrieval is genuine.

targeted_remediation.evidence: Tutor identified arithmetic as the bottleneck (turn 82 broke down subtraction) but didn't run remedial subtraction practice — just revealed 170 in turn 84.

strongest_behaviors: Diagnosing the bottleneck by asking the student to show their setup (turn 76) rather than reteaching from scratch.
Decomposing 360-190 into smaller arithmetic steps (turn 82) to reduce cognitive load.
weakest_behaviors: Foreign-language artifact in turn 72 ('强化确认：是的...') which breaks the learner experience.
Declaring mastery and moving on in turn 84 after the student never produced the correct answer themselves.

prompt_recommendations.title: Forbid non-English output
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Turn 72 produced Chinese text ('强化确认：是的，360°是正确的'), which is incomprehensible to a Seychellois S3 student.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: 强化确认：是的，360°是正确的！围绕一个点的所有角之和总是360°
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add: 'All output MUST be in English. Never emit any non-English characters or scripts. If you detect non-English tokens in your draft, regenerate in English before responding.'
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Eliminates language-mismatch failures and tool-call leakage.

prompt_recommendations.title: Suppress tool-call syntax in user-visible text
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Turn 72 leaked raw tool syntax 'call:custom:pose_question{slot:2}' to the student.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add: 'Never include tool call syntax, function names, or system markers in messages to the student. Tool calls happen separately from learner-visible text.'

prompt_recommendations.title: Require student-produced correct answer before progressing
prompt_recommendations.rationale: In turn 84 the tutor reveals 170 and moves on after the student selected wrong three times, violating mastery gating.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: Actually, $260 - 90 = 170$. You've got the method down — just a small slip... Let's try this one from the diagram.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add: 'Do not advance to a new problem until the student has produced the correct final answer themselves. After revealing a step, re-ask the original question for the student to answer.'

prompt_recommendations.title: Route repeated arithmetic errors to prerequisite practice
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Student failed basic subtraction (360-190, 260-90) three times; tutor never offered remedial subtraction practice.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: Not quite—if we add $190 + 160$, we only get to $350$.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add: 'If a student makes ≥2 arithmetic errors on a sub-step, pause the main problem and run 2-3 short prerequisite arithmetic items (e.g., simple 3-digit subtractions) before resuming.'
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Targets the real bottleneck (subtraction) instead of recycling angle problems.

prompt_recommendations.title: Vary MCQ distractors and avoid leaking the answer pattern
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Turns 78, 80, 82 reuse the same A/B/C/D set (150/160/170/180) where 160 is highlighted, anchoring the student to the wrong choice.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add: 'When re-asking after a wrong MCQ answer, change distractor values and order so the student must recompute rather than pattern-match.'

prompt_recommendations.title: Never truncate or end a tutor turn mid-sentence
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Turn 76 ends with 'In' — an incomplete sentence, confusing the student.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: Show me how you set up your calculation so I can see where it went sideways. In
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add: 'Always end with a complete sentence and an explicit question for the student. Re-read your draft before sending; if truncated, regenerate.'

prompt_recommendations.title: One instructional move per turn
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Turn 78 explains the subtraction AND poses a new MCQ in the same turn, doubling cognitive load.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: what do you get when you subtract that $190$ from $360$? If the sum of the known angles is 190°, what is the value of x?
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add: 'Each turn contains exactly ONE question to the student. Do not ask two questions in the same turn.'

prompt_recommendations.title: Interleave problem types within the topic
prompt_recommendations.rationale: All practice was 'find missing angle by subtraction'; no variation (e.g., four angles, algebraic x, straight line).
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: If three angles (90°, 100°, and x) meet at a point, what is the value of x?
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add: 'Within an angle topic, alternate problem variants: 2 unknowns, sum to 180° vs 360°, expressions like 2x, to prevent procedural mimicry.'

flow_recommendations.title: Add a regeneration check for language and tool-syntax leaks
flow_recommendations.rationale: Turn 72 emitted Chinese and a raw tool call together; an output filter would catch both.
flow_recommendations.expected_effect: Prevents leaked tool calls and non-English text reaching the student.

flow_recommendations.title: Prerequisite routing on consecutive arithmetic failures
flow_recommendations.rationale: Engine should detect that the student's errors are in subtraction, not angle reasoning, and branch into a subtraction mini-module.
flow_recommendations.evidence_quote: $260 - 90 = 170$. You've got the method down — just a small slip in the subtraction!
flow_recommendations.expected_effect: Targeted remediation on the true bottleneck.

flow_recommendations.title: Mastery gate before next-problem transition
flow_recommendations.rationale: Turn 84 transitions to a new diagram problem without the student ever producing the correct answer; gating logic should block this.
flow_recommendations.evidence_quote: Let's try this one from the diagram.
flow_recommendations.expected_effect: Enforces mastery learning at the orchestration layer.

experience_recommendations.title: Warmer, persona-aware tone for error-prone students
experience_recommendations.rationale: After three wrong tries the student gets a brisk 'Actually, …' rather than encouragement; an error-prone learner needs reassurance.
experience_recommendations.evidence_quote: Actually, $260 - 90 = 170$. You've got the method down — just a small slip in the subtraction!

experience_recommendations.title: Include the referenced diagram inline
experience_recommendations.rationale: Turn 84 says 'Let's try this one from the diagram' but no diagram is shown.
experience_recommendations.evidence_quote: Let's try this one from the diagram.

overall_summary: The session shows a reasonable retrieval-and-practice structure but is undermined by serious surface failures (non-English text and tool-call leakage in turn 72, truncations) and a critical pedagogical lapse: after the student repeatedly chose 160° due to arithmetic errors, the tutor revealed 170° and moved on rather than running prerequisite subtraction remediation or re-asking until mastery. Strengths include diagnosing via 'show me your setup' and decomposing the subtraction; weaknesses are repetitive problem type, MCQ distractor reuse, and premature progression.

bea_evaluations.skip_reason: First tutor turn; no preceding student turn.
Student posed a new question rather than making a mistake.

bea_evaluations.tutor_excerpt: That's not it — 190° is the sum of the two angles we know, but not the value of $x$. Show me how you set up your calculation so I can see where it went sideways.
bea_evaluations.rationale: Clearly identifies the error, pinpoints that 190 is the sum not x, and asks student to share setup.

bea_evaluations.mistake_description: Student stopped at 90+100 without subtracting from 360.
bea_evaluations.tutor_excerpt: Right, $90 + 100 = 190$. Since the total must be $360^\circ$, what do you get when you subtract that $190$ from $360$?
bea_evaluations.rationale: Confirms the partial work, identifies missing step (subtract from 360), and prompts the next action.

bea_evaluations.tutor_excerpt: Almost — check your subtraction of 360 - 190 one more time. What is the result?
bea_evaluations.rationale: Identifies error and asks to redo, but offers no decomposition or hint about where the subtraction went wrong.

bea_evaluations.tutor_excerpt: Not quite—if we add $190 + 160$, we only get to $350$. We need to reach $360$ for a full turn. Let's try breaking the subtraction down: $360 - 100 = 260$. Now, what is $260 - 90$?
bea_evaluations.rationale: Verifies via inverse, then decomposes the subtraction into a smaller step — strong scaffolding.

bea_evaluations.tutor_excerpt: Actually, $260 - 90 = 170$. You've got the method down — just a small slip in the subtraction! Let's try this one from the diagram.
bea_evaluations.rationale: Reveals the answer and moves on without addressing why the student keeps getting 160, no remediation on subtraction, and the next 'diagram' problem is not shown.
